# Agents Remember

> Agents Remember gives a code repository a memory in a Git repository of its own, and role agents
> that let a change land only when code and memory agree. It is the Python package
> `agents-remember-mcp`. This file summarises the documentation for a language model and links
> every page.

The links in this file are relative to the folder `docs/` of the repository
`https://github.com/Foxfire1st/agents-remember`. [Concepts](concepts.md) defines every term that
this file uses.

## The product in short

- **Tool server.** The MCP server that the command `agents-remember-mcp --config <settings file>`
  starts. A harness starts it and calls its tools. The tools stand in eight groups: server and
  context, memory, knowledge, worktrees, closeout and landing, task documents, role agents and the
  review page. The tool server also serves the skill `l-01-agent-lifecycles`, the instructions of
  the roles, to the harness as MCP resources.
- **Harness.** A coding-agent program: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes, Pi or OpenClaw. The user
  registers the tool server in a harness. The host starts a harness for each role agent.
- **Host.** The program that runs role agents and shows their chats. It is Paseo. Agents Remember
  installs a pinned version of it and starts it. The host supports Linux x86_64 only.
- **Dashboard.** The local web page that `agents-remember dashboard` serves, by default at
  `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`. It has the tabs "Chats", "Operations", "Knowledge" and "File Viewer".
- **Memory repository.** The Git repository `<coordination-root>/memory-repos/ar-<id>` of one code
  repository; `<id>` is the key of the code repository under `repositories` in the settings file.
  It holds the cards under `onboarding/`, the knowledge records under `knowledge/`, and the
  repository's own instruction and settings files under `system/`.
- **Card.** A Markdown file that describes one source file or one source folder. The card of
  `src/foo/bar.ts` is `onboarding/src/foo/bar.ts.md`. A JSON sidecar beside it holds the
  references with their anchors.
- **Knowledge record.** A JSON file under `knowledge/` that holds one shared truth with a stable ID,
  for example an invariant, a family or a decision.
- **Role agent.** A chat of a harness that the host runs in one role for one assignment. The roles
  are Architect, Investigator, Orchestrator, Manager, Worker, Reviewer, Curator and Bootstrap.
- **Task.** The unit that one Worker builds. A task belongs to a master, and a sprint groups
  masters. Tools, fields and refusals call a task a `leaf`. A task is built in an enclosure: a
  folder that holds a code worktree and a memory worktree.
- **Closeout and landing.** Closeout commits the code of a task and then its memory, after the
  knowledge gate has passed on both trees. Landing brings the closed-out work onto the branch of
  the master or of the sprint.
- **Intent review.** The review of a task's change on the review page of the dashboard. Agents
  Remember refuses every start of a role agent on a task until the task document records `go`.

## How an agent finds memory

An agent that holds a source file finds its card at the mirrored path under `onboarding/`. Two tools
name the memory that belongs to source files. `read_ar_files` names the governing card and the
knowledge records of each path it is given. `knowledge_read` names the invariants and families
attributed to one source file. Both return names and locations, never text; the agent opens the
named files itself.

## What an installation needs

A Linux x86_64 machine (WSL 2 counts as Linux), Python 3.14, uv, Git, and one harness that is
installed and logged in. Step 1 and step 4 need the network. Docker is not needed.

## Install steps

[Getting started](getting-started.md) tells these five steps in full.

1. **Install the package.** Install the published package `agents-remember-mcp` with one command:

   ```bash
   uv tool install --python 3.14 agents-remember-mcp
   ```

   The package installs the commands `agents-remember-mcp` and `agents-remember`, and it
   contains the dashboard. [Getting started](getting-started.md#1-install-the-package) also tells
   the install from a checkout of the repository.
2. **Write the settings file.** Create `~/.config/agents-remember/agents-remember-settings.json`
   with the keys `coordinationRoot`, `workspaceRoot` and `repositories`. Both roots are absolute
   paths. Each key of `repositories` is the name of a folder directly under the workspace root.
3. **Register the tool server in your harness.** The harness starts the command
   `agents-remember-mcp` with the arguments `--config` and the full path of the settings file.
   The page of each harness shows the file and the form of this declaration. Restart the harness.
4. **Start the setup.** In a chat of that harness, the agent makes one call:
   `role_start(role="bootstrap", request_id="<a new UUID>")`. The call creates the coordination
   root, installs and starts the host, starts one role agent in the role Bootstrap and starts the
   dashboard.
5. **Open the dashboard.** Open the address that the answer names in `dashboardAddress`, by
   default `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`. The setup of the repository continues in the chat of the
   Bootstrap role agent.

  the review page and the tray.

## Guides

- [Guides](guides/README.md): the index of the guides.
- [Onboard An Existing Repository](guides/onboard-existing-repo.md): set up a code repository
  that has no memory.
- [Use The Memory Repository](guides/use-external-memory.md): where the memory of a repository
  lies and how closeout keeps code and memory in step.
- [Adopt Existing Memory](guides/adopt-existing-memory.md): make the content of an existing
  memory repository the first baseline.
- [Carry Memory From a Branch](guides/carryover-from-branch.md): copy cards and knowledge
  records from the memory of another branch into an open task.
- [Refresh Stale Cards](guides/refresh-stale-onboarding.md): find and repair cards whose code
  has changed.
- [The Cost Of A Repository's First Memory](guides/cost-aware-bootstrap.md): what the first
  memory of a repository costs and the settings that choose the model of each role.
- [The review page and the explainer](guides/review-page-and-explainer.md): read the change of
  one task, ask the explainer and decide.

## Reference

- [Reference](reference/README.md): the index of the reference pages.
- [MCP Tool Reference](reference/mcp-tools.md): one row for every tool of the tool server.
- [Tool details](tool-details.md): the longer explanation of each tool whose short description
  points to it.
- [Settings Reference](reference/settings-json.md): the four settings files.
- [Harnesses and role settings](reference/harnesses.md): the harness, the model, the effort and
  the permission mode of a role.
- [Path Rules](reference/path-rules.md): which source files are eligible for cards.
- [Runtime Layout](reference/runtime-layout.md): the folders and files that an installation
  puts on disk.
- [Knowledge System](reference/knowledge-system.md): the files of the memory repository and the
  knowledge commands.
- [Memory Quality Control](reference/drift-c02.md): the checks that say whether memory is
  current and clean.
- [Worktrees And Closeout](reference/worktrees-c09.md): the worktree tools, closeout, landing
  and cleanup.
- [Product Context Resolution](reference/resolver-c08.md): how the product finds the roots, the
  memory repository and the settings of one code repository.
- [Role capsules, handovers and messages](reference/role-capsules.md): the instruction text
  that a role agent receives.
- [Skills Reference](reference/skills.md): the skills that the tool server serves.
- [Repository Certification Profiles](reference/repository-certification-profile.md): the file
  in which a repository says what a certification run executes.
- [Execution-topology authoring](reference/execution-topology.md): the fields `executionNature`
  and `executionGraph` of the task documents, which say how the masters of a sprint run and which
  of them wait for others.

  the development environment, the checks and the rules for a change.
- [Release Checklist](release-checklist.md): what a maintainer checks before a release.
- [Benchmark Methodology](benchmarks-methodology.md): how the benchmarks compare runs with and
  without memory.
- [Python test policy and commands](design/python-pytest-bootstrap.md): how the Python tests of
  the product's repository are admitted, selected and run.
- [Python Test Evidence System](design/python-evidence-system.md): how that repository sorts the
  results of its Python tests by what a result can prove.
- [Python Test Evidence Authority](design/python-test-evidence.md): which test result counts as
  acceptance.
- [The canvas host, and the review-presenter capability](design/canvas-host.md): the contracts of
  the canvas host, which serves the page of an explainer, and of the capability by whose text
  the explainer writes the page.
- [The pinned offline presentation kit](design/canvas-kit.md): the presentation kit, the
  libraries that the product ships for the pages of the explainer.
